questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework
questions.question: Why can't reranker scores be precomputed?
options: They expire faster than any cache can refresh them
They depend on the query, which changes per request
They occupy more storage than the corpus itself does
They need accelerator hardware that batch jobs lack

questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework
questions.question: Which value is inherently compute-on-read?
options: Chunk embeddings produced by the batch encoder
BM25 corpus statistics over the inverted index
Conversational query rewrites for a follow-up turn

questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework
questions.question: In the break-even arithmetic, precompute cost equals...
options: write compute plus storage plus invalidation upkeep
reads multiplied by the per-read compute they consume
storage cost minus the invalidation work it avoids
query rate multiplied by the average read latency

questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

Scores of that kind cannot be stored in warehouse tables
The reranker's interface contract forbids stored scores
Users move between service tiers too often to cache

questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

Faster dashboards with no downside for the users
Fewer invalidation jobs than the on-read version

questions.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

A streaming-only aggregate maintained per event arrival
An answer cache holding the most frequent questions
